title: CppCon 2019: Emery Berger “Mesh: Automatically Compacting Your C++ Application's Memory”
summary: Emery Berger's CppCon 2019 talk introducing Mesh, a drop-in malloc replacement that compacts memory in unmodified C and C++ programs. It tackles fragmentation by merging pages without changing pointers.
why: HN recommends Berger's talks as fascinating and cites Mesh as mind-blowing memory allocator work.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: the weird and wonderful work of Emery Berger et al with their “Mesh” malloc implementation, which blows my mind
